questionText:
Consider a sequence of 14 elements: $A = [-5, -10, 6, 3, -1, -2, 13, 4, -9, -1, 4, 12, -3, 0]$.

The subsequence sum $S(i,j) = \sum_{k=i}^{j} A[k]$. Determine the maximum of $S(i,j)$, where $0 \le i \le j < 14$. (Divide and conquer approach may be used.)
explanation:
To find the maximum subsequence sum $S(i,j)$, we need to identify the contiguous subarray that yields the highest total sum.

Step-by-step Solution:
Consider the contiguous subarray starting at index $i = 2$ and ending at index $j = 11$:
Subarray = $[6, 3, -1, -2, 13, 4, -9, -1, 4, 12]$

Sum $S(2, 11) = 6 + 3 + (-1) + (-2) + 13 + 4 + (-9) + (-1) + 4 + 12 = 29$.

No other contiguous subsequence gives a sum greater than 29. Hence, the maximum value of $S(i,j)$ is 29.
